_comment: Guided tour of the user editor. Steps point at real controls.

steps.title: Who is registered
steps.text:
Every account in the MMFDB. Listing them is an administrator operation — if the table is empty and the status line says so, that is a permission, not a fault.

The ★ column marks the account ChiSurf uses for its own database connections.

steps.title: Pick one to edit
steps.text: Select a row and the fields on the right fill in. Everything you type stays local until you save, so you can look without changing anything.

await.hint: Click any row in the table.

steps.title: You are told before the server is
steps.text: A missing display name, a malformed e-mail, a username already taken or one with spaces in it is reported above the fields as you type — not after a failed round trip.

steps.title: Rights
steps.text: Administrator allows listing, editing and deleting users; the server refuses to remove the last one. Allow sign-in without a password is convenient on a single-user machine and is not offered to administrators.

steps.title: Passwords are staged, not sent immediately
steps.text: 🔑 Password… checks the strength of what you type and holds the result until you press Save — the status line says one is waiting. Nothing is stored on this machine; the server keeps only a hash.

steps.title: Save, or throw it away
steps.text: 💾 Save writes the account back. Renaming also carries your stored session token across, so you stay signed in. ♻️ Revert discards the edits.

await.hint: Press 💾 Save when you are happy with the account.
